problemStatement: Chiro Sint-Antonius organizes an annual single-day Kubb tournament. Currently, tournament logistics — team registration, scheduling, score tracking, and standings — are managed manually or with ad-hoc tools. This leads to scheduling conflicts, delayed score updates, and a poor experience for participants trying to find their next match on the day itself. A purpose-built web application will centralize all tournament operations, provide real-time information to participants on their phones, and reduce the organizational burden on volunteers.

goalsAndObjectives.measurableOutcome: Zero double-bookings through automated conflict detection
Standings and schedule update within 60 seconds of a score entry

goalsAndObjectives.goal: Minimize admin effort on tournament day
goalsAndObjectives.measurableOutcome: Bulk import of teams, automatic schedule generation, automatic standings calculation
Single self-hosted server, no external service dependencies, offline-resilient architecture
Mobile-first public pages, no login required for viewing

targetUsers.who: One or two Chiro volunteers managing the tournament
targetUsers.access: Full access to all configuration, scheduling, scoring, and data management
targetUsers.login: Password-only authentication. Password is reset via SSH on the server.
targetUsers.keyNeeds: Set up the tournament quickly before the day, manage the schedule live, correct mistakes, export data afterward

targetUsers.who: Volunteers assigned to officiate matches across multiple fields
targetUsers.access: Score entry for any match (universal access — no per-match assignment)
targetUsers.login: Name + password, accounts created and managed by the admin
targetUsers.keyNeeds: Quickly find the current match, enter scores on a phone, move to the next match

targetUsers.who: Players and spectators at the tournament
targetUsers.access: Read-only view of the schedule, match statuses, and standings
targetUsers.keyNeeds: Find their team's next match, check live scores, view pool standings and KO bracket on a phone

requirements.title: Individual team and field management
details: Admin can add a team (name required), edit its name, or delete it
Admin can add a field, rename it, or delete it
Deletion requires a confirmation dialog

requirements.title: Bulk import
details: Text field that accepts one team name per line
Server validates for duplicates within the bulk list and against existing teams in the database
CSV upload option: first column is parsed as team name, same validation applies

requirements.title: Field generation
details: Numeric input for 'Number of fields'
Generates fields named 'Veld 1' through 'Veld N'
Existing fields are not overwritten unless the admin explicitly confirms

requirements.title: Automatic schedule generation
details: Inputs: tournament start time, average match duration, break time per round
Algorithm generates all round-robin matchups per pool
Distributes matches across time slots and fields with constraints: no team plays twice in one time slot, no field double-booked
Output: complete schedule with times, fields, and team pairings

requirements.title: Conflict check
details: On any manual modification of a match (time or field), a live validation runs
Displays a clear error if a team or field is already occupied at that time

requirements.title: Publication management
details: Toggle between 'Draft' and 'Live' status
Draft: schedule visible only to admin and referees
Live: schedule visible on the public participant pages

requirements.title: Bulk time shift
details: Admin selects a starting time slot from a dropdown
Inputs a number of minutes (positive = later, negative = earlier)
All matches from that slot onward are recalculated
Conflict check runs automatically after the shift

requirements.title: Mobile schedule overview
details: Public page showing a chronological list of matches: time, Team A vs. Team B, field
Mobile-first responsive design
Polls the API every 60 seconds for updates

requirements.title: Personal team filter
details: Search field at the top with fuzzy matching on team name
Last searched team name persisted in localStorage
On reload, automatically filters by the stored team name

requirements.title: Automatic status indicators
details: Live: current time >= match start time AND < start time + match duration, no score entered
Played: score has been entered
Awaiting result: match time has passed but no score is entered
Status is calculated client-side based on fetched data and the system clock

requirements.title: Public standings page
details: Shows pool tables with ranking: points, won, drawn, lost, goal difference
Shows KO bracket visualization with matchups and results
Same polling interval as the schedule page. No login required

requirements.title: Score entry
details: List view of matches for admin and referees
Per match: numeric input fields for Team A and Team B scores
'Save' updates the match status to 'played'
In KO phase with a draw: an additional field appears for the referee to designate the winner

requirements.title: Real-time standings calculation
details: After saving a score, the server recalculates the pool standing
Ranking order: Points > Goal difference > Head-to-head result
Standings table is updated in the database (cached Standing records)

requirements.title: Score correction
details: Admin or referee can overwrite previously entered scores
Standings are immediately recalculated after correction
In KO: winner designation can also be corrected

requirements.title: Competition type selection
details: Dropdown in tournament settings: Pools / Knockout / Combination
For Pools or Combination: automatic pool allocation (random, balanced by team count)
Manual adjustment: move teams between pools
For Combination: configure per pool how many teams advance (top 1, 2, etc.)
Pool allocation remains editable both before and after going live

requirements.title: Match logic per phase
details: Pool matches: draws are allowed
Knockout matches: draws are allowed but the referee must designate a winner via a ko_winner field
Point values (win/draw/loss) are configurable by the admin. Default: 3/1/0

requirements.title: KO bracket generation
details: Triggered by admin when pool phase is complete
Reads standings and configured number of advancing teams per pool
Seeding: random team from the top half of qualifiers vs. random team from the bottom half
Generated bracket is presented for admin review before publishing

requirements.title: KO bracket adjustment
details: Admin can swap teams or change matchups before publishing
Once published, bracket matches appear in the schedule and are assignable to fields and time slots
Subsequent KO rounds (semis, finals) are generated automatically as results come in

requirements.title: JSON export
details: Button in admin dashboard: 'Export tournament'
Downloads a .json file containing: tournament settings, teams, fields, pools, full schedule, and all results

requirements.title: JSON import
details: Button in admin dashboard: 'Import tournament'
Accepts a .json file in the same format as the export
If the database is empty: import runs directly, no confirmation needed
If data already exists: admin must confirm by entering the admin password. Existing data is fully replaced
File structure is validated before import; clear error on invalid format

requirements.title: Role-based access control
details: Two roles in the system: ADMIN and REFEREE
Participants have no account; public routes are unprotected
Server middleware enforces ADMIN on /api/admin/** routes
Server middleware enforces ADMIN or REFEREE on /api/ref/** routes

requirements.title: Authentication mechanism
details: Admin login: password field only. Validated against a bcrypt hash
Admin password reset: CLI script run via SSH on the server
Referee login: name + password fields. Accounts managed by admin
Session duration: ~12 hours (covers one tournament day)

requirements.title: Universal referee access
details: Referee dashboard shows all matches, grouped by field or time slot
Referee clicks any match to enter a score. No per-match assignment needed

performance.pageLoadTime: Public pages must load within 2 seconds on a mobile connection
performance.pollingBehavior: Pauses when the browser tab is inactive, resumes with an instant fetch when the tab becomes active

security.authentication: Session-based via Nuxt Auth Utils with bcrypt password hashing
security.networkAccess: Nginx is the only external entry point (ports 80/443). Nuxt listens on 127.0.0.1:3000 only
security.inputValidation: All user input validated server-side. Prisma parameterized queries prevent SQL injection
security.xssPrevention: User-provided strings rendered in HTML are sanitized

reliability.architecture: Single self-hosted server with no external service dependencies
reliability.backup: JSON export serves as a manual backup mechanism
reliability.restore: JSON import allows full tournament restore

usability.desktopOptimization: ~1366px wide screens. Content has a max-width with centered whitespace on wider screens
usability.language: All UI text in Dutch, managed from a centralized i18n file
usability.errorLanguage: Error messages displayed to users are in Dutch

maintainability.deployment: Manual deploy via SSH (git pull, npm run build, PM2 restart)
maintainability.testing: TDD with Vitest for API route handlers

apiNamespaces.purpose: Configuration, teams, fields, schedule, users, export/import

technicalArchitecture.stateManagement: No global store (no Pinia). Local component state via ref/reactive/computed. Shared logic via composables (useAuth, usePolling, etc.)

keyUserFlows.name: Tournament Setup (Admin)
steps: Admin logs in with password
Creates a tournament with name, start time, match duration, break time, and point values
Imports teams via bulk text or CSV
Generates fields ('Veld 1' through 'Veld N')
Selects competition type and configures pool allocation
Generates the schedule automatically
Reviews the schedule, makes manual adjustments if needed
Publishes the schedule (Draft -> Live)

keyUserFlows.name: Tournament Day — Referee
steps: Referee logs in with name + password
Sees a list of all matches
Selects a match that just finished
Enters scores for Team A and Team B
If KO phase and draw: designates the winner
Saves. Standings update automatically

keyUserFlows.name: Tournament Day — Participant
steps: Opens the public URL on their phone (no login)
Sees the full schedule sorted by time
Searches for their team name; filter is remembered on reload
Sees match statuses: upcoming, live, awaiting result, played
Navigates to standings page to view pool tables and KO bracket

keyUserFlows.name: Schedule Delay
steps: Admin notices the tournament is running behind
Selects the time slot where the delay starts
Enters the delay in minutes (e.g., +15)
System shifts all subsequent matches and runs conflict check
Participants see updated times on the next poll cycle

keyUserFlows.name: End of Tournament
steps: Admin exports the full tournament as JSON (backup/archive)
Optionally, admin can later import the JSON to restore or review the tournament

constraintsAndAssumptions: Single tournament: The system manages one tournament at a time. No multi-tournament support.
Single day: The tournament takes place in a single day. No multi-day logic needed.
Small scale: Expected ~20-40 teams, ~4-10 fields, ~50-150 matches.
Local network: Server runs on a DigitalOcean Droplet. API traffic originates from localhost via Nginx proxy.
No offline mode: Participants need an active internet connection.
Dutch only: All user-facing text is in Dutch. No multi-language support.
No real-time push: Updates via polling (60-second interval), not WebSockets.
Manual deploy: No CI/CD. Deployment via SSH.

glossary.definition: A Swedish lawn game played between two teams
A group of teams that play round-robin matches against each other
Tournament format with a pool phase followed by a knockout phase
A physical playing area where matches take place
A specific start time assigned to a match
A volunteer who officiates matches and enters scores
A player or spectator viewing the public schedule
